messages:
maria: heads-up — maintenance scheduled Sun 2026-04-12 02:00 UTC for eu-west3 GPUs. Firmware + kernel security patch. We plan staggered node drains across racks to keep at least N-1 capacity. ETA ~3h for the window.

alex: how many nodes are affected and what's the expected perf hit?

maria: ~120 GPU nodes total, we'll drain ~8 nodes per rack every 20m. Expected ~5-8% transient capacity drop in the eu-west3 pool; requests should autoscale or route to other regions.

james_oncall: @channel :rotating_light: please confirm we have a status page update and escalation path. I can own the incident page and Ops rotations during the window.

maria: thanks james — yes please make the maintenance notice and set the status page to "scheduled maintenance" one hour before start. Add a note that Dedicated customers with reserved capacity will not be affected; public-hosted tenants may see failover to other regions.

ria: I'll pin cluster-autoscaler min counts to current to avoid scale-in during drains. Also will bump scale-down delay to 30m for the window.

alex: can we pre-warm extra nodes in us-west2 to absorb spill? what's the cost delta?

tom: pre-warming a small spare pool (~16 GPUs) in us-west2 for 4h costs roughly $1.6k. Cheaper than on-demand latency impact for high-traffic routes. We can toggle it via infra CLI.

maria: prefer pre-warm vs full spill — less blast radius. Plan: pre-warm at t-30m, run a short canary workload, then enable cross-region routing.

alex: canary plan? what tests?

maria: alex will run a canary that issues multi-model gen load at current qps for 10 minutes, check latency and error rates. If green, flip routing for low-priority traffic first.

alex: got it. I'll also validate KV cache warmups for the most common prefixes to reduce token cost spike.

support-bot: status.page posted: https://status.redwood.example.com/incidents/maintenance-eu-west3-1762005123 — scheduled at 2026-04-12T02:00:00Z. Notifying Dedicated customers via email.

james_oncall: ping sales & CS with the maintenance playbook link and the list of Dedicated customers to confirm exemptions.

maria: infra ops steps (short):
```
# cordon + drain sequence per node
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# apply firmware patch job
rctl run-firmware-patch --node <node>
# uncordon
kubectl uncordon <node>
```

ria: I'll also add a temporary health-check override to avoid noisy alerts from autoscaler and to suppress non-actionable pager noise.

alex: any risk of stuck KV cache leading to higher QPS to the origin? we should watch token costs.

tom: set an alert for token-rate > 1.5x baseline for 15m — we can revert routing if it spikes. Cost hit upper bound ~+$3k for the window if things degrade and we need to route widely.

maria: communication plan:
- t-60m: status page update + #support message
- t-30m: pre-warm spare pool in us-west2
- t0: start first rack drain, run canary after first rack completes
- t+90m: reassess, proceed or pause
- t+180m: finish and confirm all nodes patched

sre-ops: I'll monitor cluster scheduling and GPU health metrics and post periodic updates in this thread during the window.

james_oncall: good — I'll create the incident channel and add CS, sales, and executive on-call. Anyone object to the time slot?

maria: no objections from infra. Chosen to hit low traffic on EU and avoid APAC business hours.

alex: thumbs-up from runtime team. I'll be on standby for canary failures.

ria: assigned to autoscaler adjustments and cooldowns.

tom: assigned to pre-warm and cost rollback if needed.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers list and creating a ticket for Dedicated exemptions.

maria: thanks everyone. Final checklist will be posted t-2h. :thumbsup:
